disease_label_per_paper: Atypical bullous erysipelas with serohematic bullae and necrosis after minor leg trauma
presentation_summary: 60-year-old woman with fibromyalgia, hypertension, and grade I obesity sustained trauma to the left leg after being struck by a rusty metal sheet.
She developed pain, burning sensation, and erythema at the injury site; left leg X-ray showed no fracture.
Initial oral clindamycin and naproxen were prescribed but not completed because symptoms rapidly worsened.
Dermatology initially diagnosed cellulitis and prescribed amoxicillin-clavulanate; after one dose, the condition deteriorated with extensive erythema and violaceous discoloration.
She was admitted the next day with rapid lesion progression, necrotic areas, bullae, and a 5 cm serohematic mass on the medial left ankle.
CBC and glucose were within normal limits; wound cultures and skin biopsy showed no significant findings.
Necrotizing fasciitis was considered due to rapid evolution and necrosis, but infectious disease made the final diagnosis of bullous erysipelas.
She improved with IV ceftriaxone followed by oral cephalexin; follow-up showed desquamation and post-inflammatory changes but persistent burning pain and decreased sensitivity.
